items.reason: Needs network: pinning 47 action refs means asking GitHub what each tag points at right now, and an invented SHA breaks a workflow rather than pinning it — the repo already has the one-command close (`npm run actions:pin`, which also flips STRICT and the P6 ratchet) and Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem to keep the pins fresh.

Already covered: issue-dispatch.yml is the workflow with the broad grant and it is already split three ways (propose holds the model key and cannot write; push holds contents:write, no secret and no network-facing input; open holds pull-requests:write and does no checkout), the ref it pushes is structurally `agent/issue-<n>` from a validated integer, and every grant is declared and justified in .github/workflow-permissions.json.

The A5 fence exists, blocks, and its vocabulary already names every family in this log; the commits land anyway because an automation lane commits in a throwaway worktree where `.husky/commit-msg` and `.husky/prepare-commit-msg` do not exist (npm install generates them, untracked). The fix is to TRACK both hooks byte-identical to the HOOKS map in scripts/install-commit-hooks.mjs — which I deliberately did not do from inside the lane whose own commit would be the first thing refused, and which would take this session's work with it.

The declaration, the installer and the blocking drift test are in; the enforced half is not, because this session is not permitted to write .claude/settings.json — one command closes it (`npm run agent:permissions -- --install`, then commit the file), after which the harness refuses a denied command instead of remembering the rule.

Needs a build: a byte or Web-Vitals ceiling has to be measured before it can be defended, and this session cannot run `next build` — an invented ceiling either fails the build or is theatre. Note the dimension is not bare: .github/perf-budgets.json already fails the required E2E job when a budgeted route's document response passes its ceiling; what is missing is the shipped-bundle half.

Already covered by `npm run test:fast` (scripts/test-fast.mjs): it selects every test whose own source names a changed file, plus the always tier in .github/test-tiers.json, reports changed files no test names, prints what it did not run, and is deliberately never a gate.

Already covered: test-llm/model-pins.json records the model surface every golden, bake and budget was accepted against (blocking via test-unit/llm-model-pin.test.mjs), and .github/workflows/llm-drift.yml re-proves the whole registry against the configured provider weekly and publishes a dated trail — the scan's premise that no model version is recorded is no longer true.

scripts/api-surface.mjs and its core existed but were unwired — no npm script and no test — so nothing compared docs/api/openapi.json to src/app/api; the comparison now runs on every build via test-unit/api-surface.test.mjs and fails on a route the spec misses, a phantom path, a moved verb list, a renamed path parameter, a changed auth posture or a TODO summary.

Every seam fence message now names the alternative design and the ADR that argued for it, and the segment-config fence — the one whose right answer was least guessable, because no-restricted-exports takes no message — gained a no-restricted-syntax twin that names the <Suspense> boundary; test-unit/lint-fences.test.mjs holds the messages to it.

lessons: This repository's fences are a coupled set, not independent files: adding a rule means a row in .github/constraint-map.json AND the matching row in AGENTS.md's table in the SAME ORDER (test-unit/constraint-map.test.mjs), and any line added to AGENTS.md needs its ceiling raised in .github/guidance-budget.json, whose ceilings are exact rather than generous. Budget two extra edits per rule you add.

Prefer wiring a new check into test:unit over adding a check:ci stage. A stage forces a gate-remedy entry, a constraint-map row and a re-measured .github/gate-timings.json baseline (cheapest-first is enforced by a clock); a test file inside the existing test:unit stage blocks just as hard with none of that coupling.

Before building anything here, check whether the repository already built it: test:fast, model-pins.json + the weekly llm-drift workflow, the three-way split of issue-dispatch.yml, and a complete-but-unwired scripts/api-surface.mjs all already existed. Roughly half of a maturity scan's findings on a repository this deliberate are either already covered or one wiring line short — and finding the half-built artefact is worth more than writing a new one.

An agent session cannot write .claude/settings.json, so a project that wants a machine-enforced tool-permission policy has to have a human or an npm install hook install it. Ship the declaration plus an installer and say plainly that the enforced half is one command away — do not claim the boundary exists.
